435

###### **WHAT HAPPENS WHEN THE APPLICATION IS APPROVED?**

###### **Grant agreement**

If a project is selected for an EU grant under Erasmus+, a grant agreement is signed between the National or Executive Agency and the applicant. The applicant will receive the grant agreement to be signed and returned to the National or Executive Agency; the National or Executive Agency is the last party to sign. When the grant is signed by both parties, the applicant becomes beneficiary of an EU grant and can start the project.

Grant agreements may take the form of mono-beneficiary agreements, with the applicant being the single beneficiary, or multi-beneficiary agreements, where all partner organisations of the consortium become beneficiaries of the agreement. The multi-beneficiary agreement is signed by the coordinator (lead applicant) which is the only contact point for the National or Executive Agency. However, all other organisations participating in a project as co-beneficiaries sign an accession form to confer on the coordinator the responsibility of acting as coordinator. In case of actions managed by National Agencies, the accession forms are combined with the declaration on honour and a mandate for the coordinator in a single document (Accession and Declaration on Honour Form). The accession forms of each partner to the coordinator should be provided at the application stage. If these accession forms are provided at a later stage, they must be made available at the latest by the time of the grant agreement signature.

**Nota bene:** Accession forms are not required for partner organisations in countries other than the country of the applicant organisation in the case of Mobility projects for Higher education students and staff, Mobility projects for learners and staff in vocational education and training, Mobility projects for pupils and staff in school education and Mobility projects for staff in adult education. However, member organisations of national consortia in the fields of higher education, VET, school and adult education are required to provide an accession form to the applicant organisation.

###### **Grant amount**

The acceptance of an application does not constitute an undertaking to award funding equal to the amount requested by the applicant. The funding requested may be reduced on the basis of the specific financial rules applying to a given Action.

The award of a grant in a given round of selection does not establish an entitlement for subsequent rounds. It should be noted that the grant amount foreseen by the agreement is a maximum which cannot be increased, even if the beneficiary requests a higher amount. If the National Agency is the granting authority, for actions using a unit cost-based model, the grant amount foreseen by the agreement could, if approved by the National Agency through an amendment, be increased using a contingency reserve to cover exceptional costs, inclusion support and/or additional units following a redistribution exercise.

Funds transferred by the Executive Agency or the National Agency must be identified within the account or sub-account indicated by the beneficiary for the payment of the grant.

###### **Payment procedures**

Depending on the type of Action, duration of the grant agreement and the assessment of financial risk, projects supported under the Erasmus+ Programme are subject to different payment procedures.

Except for the first pre-financing payment, other payments or recoveries will be made on the basis of the analysis of reports or payment requests submitted by the beneficiary (the templates of these documents will be made available in the course of the year on the websites of National Agencies or in the Funding and Tender Portal for the Executive Agency).

The payment procedures applied under Erasmus+ are described below.

###### **Pre-financing payment**

A pre-financing payment will be transferred to the beneficiary within 30 days of the date when the last of the two parties signs the grant agreement (“entry into force”), and where relevant, when any appropriate financial guarantees are

436

received (see section "financial guarantee" below). Pre-financing is intended to provide the beneficiary with a float. National Agencies or the Executive Agency may decide to split the first pre-financing payment into more instalments. They may also decide to reduce the pre-financing or not pay any pre-financing at all, if the financial capacity of the beneficiary is deemed weak.

###### **Further pre-financing payments**

Under some Actions, further pre-financing payments will be transferred to the beneficiary within 60 calendar days of the receipt, by the National Agency or the Executive Agency, of the further pre-financing payment requests advanced by the beneficiary, only if the further pre-financing payment request is accompanied by a pre-financing report. These further pre-financing payments may be requested when at least 70% of the previous pre-financing payment has been used up. Where the statement on the use of the previous pre-financing payment(s) shows that less than 70% of the previous prefinancing payment(s) has been used to cover costs of the action, the amount of the new pre-financing to be paid shall be reduced by the unused amounts of the previous pre-financing.

###### **Periodic or progress/technical reports**

Beneficiaries may be asked to submit a periodic report accompanying the request for an interim payment.

In other cases, beneficiaries can be as well requested to submit a progress report informing on the state of implementation of the project. Progress reports do not trigger a further payment. The periodic and the progress reports must be submitted by the deadline indicated in the grant agreement.

###### **Final payment or recovery of the balance**

The amount of the final payment to be made to the beneficiary will be established on the basis of a final report to be submitted by the deadline indicated in the grant agreement. If a) the events generating the grant are not implemented or are implemented in a different way than planned; or b) the eligible costs actually incurred by the beneficiary are lower than those planned at application stage, or c) the quality of the realised activities/outputs is of insufficient quality, the funding may be reduced proportionally or, where applicable, the beneficiary will be required to repay any excess amounts already received as pre-financing payment.

Under some Actions, the National or Executive Agency transfers 100% of the grant awarded through the pre-financings. In such cases a payment of the balance is not due. However, if - on the basis of a final report to be submitted by the beneficiary by the deadline indicated in the grant agreement - a) the events generating the grant are not implemented or are implemented in a different way than planned; or b) the eligible costs actually incurred by the beneficiary are lower than those planned at application stage, or c) the quality of the realised activities/outputs is of insufficient quality, the beneficiary will be required to repay any excess amounts already received as pre-financing payment.

Pre-financing payments (or parts of them) may be offset (without the beneficiaries’ consent) against amounts owed by a beneficiary to the granting authority — up to the amount due to that beneficiary.

The final payment will be issued within 60 calendar days of the receipt of the final report.

###### **OTHER IMPORTANT PROVISIONS**

###### **EU values, grave professional misconduct, and conflict of interest**

The applicants need to be aware that if they are awarded the grant, the grant agreement obliges the involved parties to carry out the action in line with the highest ethical standards and the applicable EU, international and national law on ethical principles. During the implementation of the action, the beneficiaries must commit to and ensure the respect of EU values (such as respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and human rights, including the rights of minorities). In case of breach, the granting authority may reduce or recover the grant and terminate the grant agreement.

437

Incitement to discrimination, hatred or violence against a group of persons or a member of a group, or similar activities that are contrary to the values on which the Union is founded, as enshrined in Article 2 of the Treaty on European Union<sup>506</sup> , are unacceptable and incompatible with the values and objectives of the programme, regardless of whether such actions occur before, during or after project implementation. In line with EU Financial Regulation, such behaviour can qualify as a ground for exclusion from EU funds where it has been established by a final judgment or a final administrative decision that the person or entity is guilty of grave professional misconduct by having violated applicable laws or regulations or ethical standards of the profession to which the person or entity belongs, or by having engaged in any wrongful conduct which has an impact on its professional credibility where such conduct denotes wrongful intent or gross negligence<sup>507</sup> . Excluded entities cannot receive EU funds<sup>508</sup> .

The applicants should also take note that after the grant is awarded and grant agreement signed, they must take all measures to prevent any conflict of interests where the impartial and objective implementation of the agreement could be compromised for reasons involving family, emotional life, political or national affinity, economic interest or any other direct or indirect interest. They must formally notify the granting authority without delay of any situation constituting or likely to lead to a conflict of interests and immediately take all the necessary steps to rectify this situation. The granting authority may verify that the measures taken are appropriate and may require additional measures to be taken by a specified deadline. The same obligation to prevent any situation of conflict of interest applies to subcontractors.

Overall, the action must be implemented by the participating organisations as described in their application and in compliance with the provisions of the grant agreement, the call conditions, the applicable quality standards, as well as all legal obligations under applicable EU, international and national law.

###### **Financial guarantee**

If the financial capacity is considered weak, the National or Executive Agency may require any beneficiary which has been awarded a grant exceeding EUR 60 000 to provide a guarantee in advance in order to limit the financial risks connected with the pre-financing payment. This guarantee can be requested for up to the same amount of the pre-financing payment(s).

The purpose of such guarantee is to make a bank or financial institution stand as irrevocable collateral security or firstcall guarantor of the beneficiary’s obligations deriving from the grant agreement.

This financial guarantee, in euro, shall be provided by an approved bank or financial institution established in an EU Member State. When the beneficiary is established in a non-EU country, the National or Executive Agency may agree that a bank or financial institution established in such country provides the guarantee, if it considers that the bank or financial institution offers equivalent financial security and characteristics as those offered in an EU Member State.

The guarantee may be replaced by a joint third-party guarantee, or from several third-party guarantees from the participating organisations who are parties to the same grant agreement.

The guarantee will be released after the pre-financing is gradually cleared against an interim payment or payment of the balance to the beneficiary, in accordance with the conditions laid down in the grant agreement. In case the payment of the balance takes the form of a recovery, either the guarantee will be released after the beneficiary is notified or will remain explicitly in force until the final payment and, if the final payment takes the form of a recovery, until three months after the debit note is notified to a beneficiary.

###### **Subcontracting and award of procurement contract**

In principle, limited subcontracting of services is allowed, provided it does not cover core activities on which the achievement of the objectives of the action directly depends. As a rule, tasks performed by the coordinator under the

> 506 <u>https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:12012M002</u> 507 Article 138 (1) c) vi) of the EU Financial Regulation

> 508 For more details, see exclusion criteria section

438

grant agreement cannot be subcontracted<sup>509</sup> . The beneficiary may resort to subcontracting for non-core activities, such as specific technical services, which are part of the action tasks, requiring specialised skills (relating to the legal, accounting, tax, human resources fields, IT, etc.) or implementation contracts. The costs incurred by the beneficiary for this type of services may therefore be considered eligible costs provided they meet all the other criteria described in the grant agreement, such as best value for money and absence of conflict of interest.

Where implementation of the project requires the procurement of goods, works or services (contract), beneficiaries must award the contract to the economically most advantageous offer, i.e. the bid offering the best value for money, or, as appropriate to the tender offering the lowest price, ensuring that there is no conflict of interest and that documentation is retained in case of audit.

In the event of implementation contract exceeding a value of EUR 60 000, the National or Executive Agency may impose special rules on the beneficiary, in addition to those referred to in the previous paragraph. Those special rules would be published on the websites of the National Agencies or the Executive Agency.

###### **Information on the grants awarded**

In line with the principle of transparency and the requirement for ex-post publicity, information on the recipients of the Union funds must be published on the website of the Commission, the Executive Agency and/or the National Agencies during the first half of the year following the closure of the financial year for which they were awarded.

The information may also be published in any other appropriate medium, including the Official Journal of the European Union.

The National Agencies and the Executive Agency will publish the following information:

- name and locality of the beneficiary;

- amount of grant awarded;

- nature and purpose of the award.

Upon a reasoned and duly substantiated request by the beneficiary, the publication shall be waived if such disclosure risks threatening the rights and freedoms of individuals concerned as protected by the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union or harm the commercial interests of the beneficiaries.

As far as personal data referring to natural persons are concerned, the information published shall by removed two years after the end of the financial year in which the funds were awarded.

The same shall apply to personal data indicated in the official titles of legal persons (e.g. an association or company having as title the names of their founders).

This information shall not be published for scholarships paid to natural persons and other direct support paid to natural persons in most need (refugees and unemployed persons). Also, the beneficiary organisations are not authorised to publish this type of information in relation to persons receiving a mobility grant under Erasmus+.

###### **Visibility of Union action**

Specific requirements regarding the visibility of the project, sharing of project results and project impact, as well as the obligation to ensure publicity for each granted project are detailed in the particular calls/actions and grant agreements. Beneficiaries must clearly acknowledge the European Union’s support in all communications or publications, in whatever form or whatever medium, including the Internet, or on the occasion of activities for which the grant is used. This must

> 509 In case of public bodies, coordinators may delegate some of their tasks as per grant agreement to an entity with ‘authorisation to administer’.

439

be done according to the provisions included in the call and the grant agreement. If these provisions are not fully complied with, the beneficiary’s grant may be reduced.

###### **Checks, audits and monitoring**

The National or Executive Agency and/or the European Commission may carry out technical and financial checks and audits in relation to the use of the grant.

Where issues are encountered in a particular project or for a given participant (for example operational or financial capacity issues), these might require closer monitoring and taking of measures as described in the grant agreement. The purpose of such monitoring is to help the beneficiaries manage risk so that it does not materialise and the action can be successfully finalised. The granting authority may also check the statutory records of the beneficiary (or co-beneficiary) for the purpose of periodic assessments of lump sum, unit cost or flat-rate financing. The beneficiary (or co-beneficiary) will undertake, with the signature of its legal representative, to provide proof that the grant has been used correctly. The European Commission, the Executive Agency, National Agencies and/or the European Court of Auditors, OLAF, EPPO or a body mandated by them, may check the use made of the grant at any time up to five years, or for up to three years for grants not exceeding EUR 60 000, after final payment. Therefore, beneficiaries shall keep records, original supporting documents, statistical records and other documents connected with the grant during this period.

Different types of audit procedures may be applied according to the type of Action concerned, the size of the grant awarded and the form of the grant.

The detailed provisions concerning checks and audits are described in the grant agreement.

###### **Risk assessment and monitoring**

Risk assessment is a fundamental part of managing EU grants, as it helps to safeguard public funds, enhance project success, and promote accountability and transparency. It is a critical component of both the application process and the management of EU funded projects and helps to ensure that funds are allocated and used effectively, efficiently, and in compliance with the relevant policies and regulations.

Risk identification and mitigation is often required from applicants when preparing their applications. It is also relevant at the stage of project selection. The EU Financial Regulation allows the authorising officer in several instances to waive an obligation or request additional documents from an applicant based on its risk assessment. Some actions also require the applicants to present a risk management plan, and where this is the case, the plan itself is part of the project’s evaluation. Finally, risk monitoring relating to the beneficiary and the project takes place during project implementation in the context of checks, reviews, audits or investigations carried out under a particular grant agreement.

###### **Collaboration and consistent Programme implementation through information technology system used by the Commission, EACEA and National Agencies**

In order to ensure consistent implementation of the Programme across all participating countries<sup>510</sup> and the protection of EU financial interests<sup>511</sup> , the information concerning the applicant, the application, compliance with eligibility and exclusion criteria, the related operational and financial capacity assessments and other relevant information, including on previously funded projects and, if the grant is awarded, information concerning the implementation of the project and any reinforced monitoring thereof, can be made accessible to authorised persons of the European Commission, EACEA and the National Agencies in the context of selection and award, prevention of double funding, monitoring, and other instances in the context of supervisory controls and primary checks pursuant to Erasmus+ Regulation.

All access to information is subject to rules of personal Data Protection notice specified below.

> 510 See Article 128 of the EU Financial regulation as well as Article 28(7) and (8) of the Erasmus+ Regulation.

> 511 See in particular Article 194 of the EU Financial Regulation on the prohibition of double funding.

440

Concerning the EACEA, data can be made accessible through the Funding and Tenders Portal in line with the applicable privacy statements<sup>512</sup> . The sharing of information between EACEA and the National Agencies must comply with the provisions of the Memorandums of Understanding signed between them.

###### **Protection of the financial interests of the Union**

The Commission takes appropriate measures to ensure that, when actions financed under the Erasmus+ Regulation are implemented, the financial interests of the Union are protected by the application of preventive measures against fraud, corruption and any other illegal activities by effective controls and, if irregularities are detected, by the recovery of the amounts wrongly paid and, where appropriate, by effective, proportionate and dissuasive administrative and financial penalties<sup>513</sup> . This includes carrying out supervisory controls with regard to the Programme actions and activities managed by the national agencies, setting the minimum requirements for the controls by national agencies and independent audit bodies, processing of data as described below, and cooperating closely with the national agencies who are responsible for the primary controls of grant beneficiaries.

Applicants for grants need to be aware that any person or entity receiving Union funds is required to fully cooperate in the protection of the financial interests of the Union and shall, as a condition for receiving the funds, grant the necessary rights and access required for the authorising officer responsible, for the EPPO in respect of those Member States participating in enhanced cooperation pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2017/1939, for OLAF, for the Court of Auditors, and, where appropriate, for the relevant national authorities, to comprehensively exert their respective competences<sup>514</sup> .

###### **Data protection**

Any personal data included in the application form or in the grant agreement shall be processed by the National or Executive Agency, or by the European Commission in accordance with:

- For all processing that is required by any official guidance or instructions from the European Commission or necessary for the implementation of the Erasmus+ Programme: Regulation (EU) 2018/1725 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 October 2018<sup>515</sup> on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data by the Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies and on the free movement of such data, and repealing Regulation (EC) No 45/2001 and Decision No 1247/2002/EC (Text with EEA relevance.);

- For all processing for other purposes, not required by any official guidance or instructions from the European Commission nor necessary for the implementation of the Erasmus+ Programme:

- the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR or EU Regulation 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 April 2016<sup>516</sup> ) for:

- all personal data processed by a controller or processor in the EU/EEA;

- all personal data on data subjects who are in the EU/EEA at the start of the processing;

- the national data protection legislation for all other processing.

In these cases, the entity deciding on the means and purposes of the processing for these other purposes shall replace the European Commission as accountable and responsible Data Controller under their applicable data protection legislation.

Unless marked as optional, the applicant's replies to the questions in the application form are necessary to evaluate and further process the grant application in accordance with the Erasmus+ Programme Guide. Personal data will be processed solely for that purpose by the department or Unit responsible for the Union grant programme concerned (entity acting

as data controller). Personal data may be transferred on a need-to-know basis to third parties involved in the evaluation of applications or in the grant management procedure, without prejudice of transfer to the bodies in charge of monitoring and inspection tasks in accordance with European Union law or to bodies mandated to undertake evaluations of the Programme or any of its Actions. In particular, for the purposes of safeguarding the financial interests of the Union, personal data may be transferred to internal audit services, to the European Court of Auditors, to the Financial Irregularities Panel, to the European Anti-Fraud Office or to the European Public Prosecutor's Office and between authorising officers of the Commission and the executive agencies. The applicant shall have the right of access to their personal data and the right to rectify any such data. In case of conflicts, the applicant also has the right of recourse at any time to the European Data Protection Supervisor.

Concerning the processing of personal data under the Erasmus+ Programme, a detailed privacy notice, including contact information for any queries concerning the processing of their personal data, is available here: <u>www.webgate.ec.europa.eu/erasmus-esc/index/privacy-statement</u>

The applicant shall inform the individuals whose personal data is contained in the proposal of the relevant privacy statement as indicated above, before submitting their proposals.

## **– PART D GLOSSARY OF TERMS**

This section presents definitions of key concepts related to the Erasmus+ Programme. The glossary is divided into sections organised in alphabetical order, covering both common terms as well as specific concepts only relevant to a given sector.

#### **Common terms**

|**Accompanying person**|A person who accompanies participants (learners, staff, young people or<br>youth workers) in a mobility activity in order to ensure their safety, provide<br>support and assistance, as well as assist with the participant’s effective<br>learning during the mobility experience. In individual activities, an<br>accompanying<br>person<br>may<br>accompany<br>participants<br>with<br>fewer<br>opportunities or minors and young people with little experience outside<br>their own country. In case of group activities in the field of education and<br>training, qualified education staff must accompany the group to facilitate<br>the learning process.|
|---|---|
|**Accreditation**|Administrative procedure to ensure that the organisations wishing to have<br>simplified access to Erasmus+ funding under an Action comply with a set of<br>criteria and minimum requirements. The award of an accreditation<br>represents the first stage in a two-stage submission procedure for certain<br>grants and does not trigger an immediate award of funding under the<br>Erasmus+ Programme.|
|**Affiliated entity**|The following can be considered affiliated entities (in accordance with<br>Article 190 of the Financial Regulation):<br>•<br>legal entities having a legal or capital link with beneficiaries; this<br>link is neither limited to the action nor established for the sole<br>purpose of its implementation;<br>•<br>several entities which satisfy the criteria for being awarded a grant<br>and together form one entity which may be treated as the sole<br>beneficiary, including where the entity is specifically established<br>for the purpose of implementing the action.<br>Affiliated entities must comply with the eligibility and non-exclusion criteria,<br>and where applicable also with the selection criteria applying to applicants<br>but they do not count toward the minimum eligibility criteria for the<br>consortium composition(if any).|
|**Applicant**|A natural person or an entity with or without legal personality who has<br>submitted an application in a grant award procedure, including any<br>participating organisation or informal group of young people.<br>Applicants may apply either individually or on behalf of other organisations<br>involved in the project. In the latter case, the applicant is also defined as<br>coordinator.<br>For actions managed by the Executive Agency EACEA, the applicants are<br>those entities who will become beneficiaries and affiliated entities in the<br>Grant Agreement if their application is funded.|
|**Application deadline**|Final date for submission of the application to the National or Executive<br>Agencyto be considered admissible.|

443

|**Associated partners**|Entities from the public or private sector that contribute to the<br>implementation of specific project tasks/activities or support the promotion<br>and sustainability of the project, but that for contractual management<br>aspects are not considered to be beneficiaries, and do not receive any<br>funding from the Programme as part of the project (they do not have the<br>right to charge costs or claim contributions.).|

Calls for proposals are<br>published in the Official Journal of the European Union (C series) and/or on<br>relevant websites of the Commission,National or Executive Agency.|

|**Co-financing**|The principle under which part of the costs of a project supported by the EU<br>must be borne by the beneficiary or covered through external contributions<br>other than the EUgrant.|

It includes information and data literacy, communication and<br>collaboration, media literacy, digital content creation (including<br>programming), safety (including digital well-being and competences related<br>to cybersecurity), intellectual property related questions, problem solving<br>and critical thinking.|

The platform<br>interconnects with national data sources for learning opportunities and<br>nationalqualifications databases or registers.|
|**European NGO**|For the purpose of this programme, these are NGOs that operate through a<br>formally recognised structure composed of a European body/secretariat<br>legally established for at least two years in an EU Member State or third<br>country<br>associated<br>to<br>the<br>Programme<br>and<br>of<br>national<br>organisations/branches, in at least nine EU Member States and third<br>countries<br>associated<br>to<br>the<br>Programme.<br>These<br>national<br>organisations/branches must:<br>•<br>have<br>a<br>proven<br>statutory<br>link<sup>518</sup><br>with<br>the<br>European<br>body/secretariat;<br>•<br>be active in the field of education, training or youth.<br>A European NGO must be composed of at least nine entities (the European<br>body/secretariat and at least eight national organisations/branches)<br>established in nine different EU Member States and third countries<br>associated to the Programme.|
|**First time applicant**|Any participating organisation that has not previously received support as a<br>project coordinator (applicant) under a given type of action supported by<br>this Programme or itspredecessorprogramme in the last sevenyears.|

> 517 In case of doubt, see Article 11 of Regulation (EC) No 987/2009 for elements determining residence.

> 518 Defined under the term “statutory link” in this Glossary.

445

|**Force majeure**|Any situation or event that prevents organisations and individuals from<br>fulfilling their obligations in the implementation of the project activities.<br>This situation or event has to be unforeseeable, exceptional situation and<br>beyond the parties’ control. The force majeure cannot be due to error or<br>negligence of the organisations or other participants involved in the action,<br>andproves to be inevitable in spite of exercisingall due diligence.|
|---|---|
|**Green skills**|Competences and knowledge necessary to the transition to a low-carbon<br>economy, which can be general such as sustainable agriculture, soil<br>protection, energy use and waste reduction, or more technical such as<br>knowledge on renewable energy.|
|**Green travel**|Travel that uses low emissions means of transport for at least half of the<br>round trip, such as bus, train, bike, or car-pooling. Traveling by boat will be<br>considered as green travel if combined with other low-emissions means of<br>transport.|
|**Hosting / receiving**<br>**organisation**|The (main) organisation that provides learning content to participants in<br>mobility activities by using its own resources and expertise. The hosting<br>organisation cooperates with the sending organisation to define the<br>expected learning outcomes and the methods that will be used to achieve<br>them. It then executes the learning programme and conducts monitoring<br>and mentoringduringthe activity.|
|**Informal learning**|Learning resulting from daily activities and experiences which is not<br>organised or structured in terms of objectives, time or learning support; it<br>maybe unintentional from the learner’sperspective.|
|**International**|In the context of Erasmus+, relates to any action involving at least one EU<br>Member State or third country associated to the Programme and at least<br>one third countrynot associated to the Programme.|
|**Job shadowing**|A stay at a partner organisation in another country with the aim of receiving<br>training by following practitioners in their daily work in the receiving<br>organisation, exchanging good practices, acquiring skills and knowledge<br>and/or buildinglong-termpartnerships throughparticipative observation.|
|**Key competences**|The basic set of knowledge, skills and attitudes which all individuals need<br>for personal fulfilment and development, employability, social inclusion,<br>sustainable lifestyle, successful life in peaceful societies, health-conscious<br>life management and active citizenship, as described in the Council<br>Recommendation 2018/C 189/01 of 22 May 2018 on key competences for<br>lifelonglearning.|
|**Learning mobility**|Moving physically to a country other than the country of residence in order<br>to undertake study,trainingor non-formal or informal learning.|
|**Learning outcomes**|Statements of what a participant knows, understands and is able to do on<br>completion of a learning process, which are defined in terms of knowledge,<br>skills and competence.|
|**Legal entity**|A natural person or a legal person created and recognised as such under<br>national law, Union law or international law which has legal personality and<br>which may, acting in its own name, exercise rights and be subject to<br>obligations, or an entity which does not have legal personality as referred<br>to inpoint(c)of Article 200(2)of the Financial Regulation.|

446

|**Legal Entity Appointed**<br>**Representative (LEAR)**|For action managed by the European Education and Culture Executive<br>Agency, parallel to the validation of an organisation in the Participant<br>Register, its legal representative(s) must nominate a Legal Entity Appointed<br>Representative (LEAR). The LEAR role, is key: once validated by the<br>Commission, the LEAR will be authorised to:<br>•<br>manage the legal and financial information about the organisation<br>•<br>manage access rights of persons in the organisation (but not at the<br>project level)<br>•<br>appoint representatives of the organisation to electronically sign grant<br>agreements ('Legal Signatories' - LSIGN) or financial statements<br>('Financial Signatories' - FSIGN) via the Funding & Tenders Portal.<br>All the steps for the LEAR validation are clarified in the Funding & Tenders<br>Portal.|
|---|---|
|**Less experienced**<br>**organisation**|Any participating organisation that has not received support in a given type<br>of action supported by this Programme or its predecessor programme more<br>than twice in the last seven years. This category includes the category of<br>“first-time applicants”,as defined above.|
|**Life-long learning**|Learning in all its forms, whether formal, non-formal or informal, taking<br>place at all stages in life and resulting in an improvement or update in<br>knowledge, skills, competences and attitudes or participation in society<br>from a personal, civic, cultural, social or employment-related perspective,<br>including the provision of counselling and guidance services; it includes<br>early childhood education and care, general education, vocational<br>education and training, higher education, adult education, youth work and<br>other learning settings outside formal education and training and it typically<br>promotes cross-sectoral cooperation and flexible learning pathways.|
|**Newcomer organisation**|Any participating organisation that has not previously received support in a<br>given type of action supported by this Programme or its predecessor<br>programme either as a coordinator or apartner.|
|**Micro-credential**|A micro-credential is a recognised proof of the learning outcomes that a<br>learner has achieved following a short learning experience, according to<br>transparent standards and requirements and upon assessment.<br>The proof is contained in a certified document that lists the name of the<br>holder, the achieved learning outcomes, the assessment method, the<br>awarding body and, where applicable, the qualifications framework level<br>and the credits gained. Micro-credentials are owned by the learner, are<br>shareable, portable and may be combined into larger credentials or<br>qualifications.|
|**Mobility/Learning**<br>**agreement**|An agreement between the sending and receiving organisation and the<br>participating individuals, defining the aims and content of the mobility<br>period in order to ensure its relevance and quality. It can also be used as a<br>basis for recognition of theperiod abroad bythe receivingorganisation.|
|**Month**|For thepurpose of calculatingthegrants,a month is equal to 30 days.|

447

|**MOOC (Massive Open Online**<br>**Course)**|A type of course that is completely delivered online, is open to be accessed<br>by anyone without cost, entry qualifications or other restrictions;<br>participant numbers are often high. These courses can have in-person<br>components, e.g. encouraging local participant meetings, and formal<br>assessment, but tend to use peer review, self-assessment and automated<br>grading. There are many variations of MOOCs, focused on specific sectors,<br>target groups (e.g. vocational focus, teachers, etc.) or teaching methods.<br>MOOCs funded under Erasmus+ have to be open to all and both the<br>participation and a certificate or badge of completion are free of charge for<br>participants. The open access requirement for educational resources<br>applies also to MOOCs and other complete courses.|
|---|---|
|**National Agency**|A designated body in charge of managing the implementation of the<br>Programme at national level in a Member State or in a third country<br>associated to the Programme. One or more National Agencies may exist in<br>each country.|
|**National Authority**|An authority in charge, at national level, of monitoring and supervising the<br>management of the Programme in a Member State or in a third country<br>associated to the Programme. One or more National Authorities may exist<br>in each country.|
|**Non-formal learning**|Learning which takes place through planned learning activities where some<br>form of learning support is present, but which is not part of the formal<br>education and trainingsystem.|
|**Occupational profile**|The set of skills, competences, knowledge and qualifications that is usually<br>relevant for a specific occupation.|
|**OID (Organisation ID)**|A unique number that corresponds to an organisation. This number can be<br>used when applying for an accreditation or grant under the Erasmus+ and<br>European SolidarityCorps actions managed byNational Agencies.|
|**Open Access**|Making grant outputs, such as publishing materials freely accessible to the<br>public without restrictions, typically through digital platforms and<br>repositories. Erasmus+ has an Open Access Requirement for educational<br>resources and encourages Open Access of research results and data.|
|**Open Educational Resources**<br>**(OER)**|Educational materials of any kind (e.g., textbooks, worksheets, lesson plans,<br>instructional videos, entire online courses, educational games) which can be<br>freely used, adapted and shared. OERs have either been released under an<br>open license or are in the public domain (i.e., copyright protection has<br>expired). Cost-free materials that cannot be adapted and shared by the<br>public are not OERs.|
|**Open licence**|A way for copyright holders (creators or other rightsholders) to grant the<br>general public the legal permission to freely use their work. Under the<br>Erasmus+ Open Access Requirement, any such open license must permit at<br>least use, adaptation and distribution. The open license should be indicated<br>on the work itself or wherever the work is distributed. Educational materials<br>with an open license are called Open Educational Resources(OERs).|
|**Participant in Erasmus+**<br>**project activities**|Individual who is fully involved in a project and who may receive European<br>Union funding intended to cover the costs of participation (notably travel<br>and subsistence).|
|**Participating organisation**|An organisation or informal group of young people involved in an Erasmus+<br>project,as either coordinator orpartner.|
|**Partner organisation**|In actions managed by National Agencies, an organisation formally involved<br>in theproject(co-beneficiaries)but not takingthe role of coordinator.|
|**Partnership**|An agreement between a group of institutions or organisations to carry out<br>joint activities andprojects.|

448

|**Participant with fewer**<br>**opportunities**|People with fewer opportunities means people who, for economic, social,<br>cultural, geographical or health reasons, a migrant background, or for<br>reasons such as disability and educational difficulties or for any other<br>reasons, including those that can give rise to discrimination under article 21<br>of the Charter of Fundamental rights of the European Union, face obstacles<br>that prevent them from having effective access to opportunities under the<br>programme.|
|---|---|
|**Peer Learning**|A reciprocal learning activity, which is mutually beneficial and involves the<br>sharing of knowledge, ideas and experience between the participants. Peer<br>learning practices enable to interact with other participants, their peers,<br>and participate in activities where they can learn from each other and meet<br>educational, professional and/orpersonal developmentgoals.|
|**Professional development**|Process of enhancing the professional capabilities of participants (learners<br>and staff) by developing competences and expertise and acquiring new<br>skills, which are normally identified in a development needs analysis.<br>Professional development encompasses all types of learning opportunities,<br>ranging from structured trainings and seminars to informal learning<br>opportunities.|
|**Profit-making body active in**<br>**corporate social**<br>**responsibility**|An organisation active in corporate social responsibility which integrates<br>social, environmental, and ethical concerns into its strategies and core<br>operations alongside its financial goals, and demonstrates substantial<br>experience in the youth sector, provided its involvement in activities funded<br>under this Programme does not have a commercial purpose and is not aimed<br>atgenerating profit.|
|**Project**|A coherent set of activities which are designed and organised in order to<br>achieve defined objectives and results.|
|**Qualification**|A formal outcome of an assessment and validation process which is<br>obtained when a competent body determines that an individual has<br>achieved learningoutcomes togiven standards.|
|**Receiving organisation**|A participating organisation receiving participants and organising activities<br>of an Erasmus+project.|
|**School**|An institution providing general, vocational or technical education, at any<br>level from pre-school to upper secondary education, including early<br>childhood education and care. To verify eligibility under the field of ‘school<br>education’, please consult the definition of eligible schools in each country<br>on the website of the relevant National Agency.|
|**School pupil**|A person enrolled in a learning capacity at an institution providing general<br>education at any level from early childhood education and care to upper<br>secondary education, or a person schooled outside an institutional setting<br>considered by the competent authorities as eligible to participate in the<br>Programme in their respective territories.|
|**Sending organisation**|A participating organisation sending one or more participants to an activity<br>of an Erasmus+project.|
|**Small and medium-sized**<br>**enterprises (SMEs)**|Enterprises (see definition above) which employ fewer than 250 people and<br>which have an annual turnover not exceeding 50 million EUR, and/or an<br>annual balance sheet total not exceeding43 million EUR.|

449

|**Social enterprise**|An undertaking, irrespective of its legal form, which is not listed on a<br>regulated market within the meaning of Article 4(21) of Directive<br>2014/65/EU, and which: 1) in accordance with its articles of association,<br>statutes or any other statutory document establishing the business, has as<br>its primary objective the achievement of measurable, positive social impacts<br>rather than generating profit for its owners, members and stakeholders,<br>where the undertaking: a) provides innovative services or goods which<br>generate a social return and/or b) employs an innovative method of<br>production of goods or services and that method of production embodies<br>its social objective; 2) reinvests its profits first and foremost to achieve its<br>primary objective and has in place predefined procedures and rules for any<br>circumstances in which profits are distributed to shareholders and owners,<br>in order to ensure that any distribution of profits does not undermine the<br>primary objective; 3) is managed in an entrepreneurial, accountable and<br>transparent way, in particular by involving workers, customers and/or<br>stakeholders affected byits business activities.|
|---|---|
|**Staff**|A person who, on either a professional or a voluntary basis, is involved in<br>education, training or non-formal learning at all levels. Includes professors,<br>teachers (including pre-school teachers), trainers, school leaders, youth<br>workers, sport staff, early childhood education and care staff, non-<br>educational staff and other practitioners involved on a regular basis in<br>promotinglearning.|
|**Statutory link**|The cooperation between the organisations concerned is based on a<br>formalised/documented relation, which is neither limited to the project<br>they apply for, nor established for the sole purpose of its implementation.<br>This link can cover many forms, from a very integrated one (e.g., one<br>“mother organisation" with its national branches/affiliated entities with or<br>without proper legal entity) to a looser one (e.g., a network functioning<br>through a clearly defined membership modality requiring for instance: the<br>payment of a fee, the signature of a membership contract/agreement, the<br>definition of rights and obligations from the twoparties,etc.).|
|**Study visit**|A trip where the participant gets to know and study another organisation or<br>institution, its practices and systems. It enables the participant to have a<br>learning experience based on direct contact and on observation of the host<br>organisation’s methods andpractices.|
|**Third countries not**<br>**associated to the**<br>**Programme**|Third countries not associated to the Programme are countries which do not<br>have an agreement signed with the Union pursuant to Article 19 of the<br>Erasmus+ Regulation. Pursuant to Article 20 of this Regulation, in duly<br>justified cases in the Union’s interest, the actions referred to in Articles 5 to<br>7, points (a) and (b) of Article 8 and Articles 9 to 14 of Erasmus+ Regulation<br>may also be open to participation of legal entities of third countries not<br>associated to the Programme. No National Agency is established in these<br>countries. The list of third countries not associated to the Programme<br>whose legal entities may apply to Erasmus+ calls is set out in Part A of this<br>Guide in the section "Who can participate in the Erasmus+ Programme?".<br>Decision to award a grant to such entities is made by the authorising officer<br>on a case-by-case basis, having regard to the justification of the Union’s<br>interest.|
|**Traineeship (work**<br>**placement)**|Time spent in an enterprise or organisation in another country, with a view<br>to acquiring specific competences that are needed by the labour market,<br>gaining work experience and acquiring more understanding of the economic<br>and social culture of that country.|

450

|**Transnational**|In the context of Erasmus+, relates, unless otherwise indicated, to any<br>activity involving at least two EU Member States and third countries<br>associated to the Programme.|
|---|---|
|**Transversal (soft; life) skills**|Include the ability to think critically, be curious and creative, to take<br>initiative, to solve problems and work collaboratively, to be able to<br>communicate<br>efficiently<br>in<br>a<br>multicultural<br>and<br>interdisciplinary<br>environment, to be able to adapt to context and to cope with stress and<br>uncertainty. These skills arepart of the keycompetences.|
|**Union transparency and**<br>**recognition tools**|Instruments to help stakeholders understand, appreciate and, where<br>appropriate, recognise learning outcomes and qualifications throughout the<br>European Union.|
|**Validation of non-formal and**<br>**informal learning**|A process of confirmation by an authorised body that an individual has<br>acquired learning outcomes measured against a relevant standard and<br>consists of the following four distinct phases:<br>1. Identification through dialogue of particular experiences of an individual;<br>2. Documentation to make visible the individual's experiences;<br>3. A formal assessment of these experiences; and<br>4. Certification of the results of the assessment which may lead to a partial<br>or fullqualification|
|**Venue**|Thephysical location where an activityis taking place.|
|**Virtual cooperation**|Any form of cooperation using information and communication technology<br>tools to facilitate and support anyrelevant Programme actions.|
|**Virtual learning**|Acquisition of knowledge, skills and competences through the use of<br>information and communication technology tools that allow participants to<br>have a meaningful transnational or international learningexperience.|
|**Work Package**|A component of the project work breakdown. It represents a group of<br>project activities targetingcommon specific objectives.|
|**Young people**|In the context of the Erasmus+ Programme, individuals aged between 13<br>and 30.|

###### **Higher Education**

|**Credit**|A set of learning outcomes of an individual which have been assessed and<br>which can be accumulated towards a qualification or transferred to other<br>learning programmes orqualifications.|
|---|---|
|**Credit mobility**|A limited period of study or traineeship abroad set within on-going studies<br>at a home institution - for the purpose of gaining credits. After the mobility<br>phase, students return to their home institution to complete their studies.|
|**Degree mobility**|A period of study abroad aimed at acquiring a full degree or certificate in the<br>destination country/ies.|
|**Diploma Supplement**|An annex to the official qualification documentation, which is designed to<br>provide more detailed information on the studies completed according to an<br>agreed format, which is internationally recognized; a document<br>accompanying a higher education diploma, providing a standardised<br>description of the nature, level, context, content and status of the studies<br>completed by its holder. It is produced by higher education institutions<br>according to standards agreed by the European Commission, the Council of<br>Europe and UNESCO. In the context of an international joint study<br>programme, it is recommended to deliver a "joint diploma supplement"<br>covering the entire programme and endorsed by all the degree awarding<br>universities.|

451

|**Double**<br>**degree/multiple**<br>**degree**|(At least) two separate degree certificates awarded to a student upon<br>successful completion of a joint programme. A double degree is a specific<br>type of multiple degree. Each degree must be signed by the competent<br>authority of the institution concerned, and recognised officially in the<br>countries where the different awarding institutions are located.|
|---|---|
|**ECHE (Erasmus Charter for**<br>**Higher Education)**|An accreditation granted by the European Commission giving the possibility<br>to higher education institutions from EU Member States and third countries<br>associated to the Programme to be eligible to apply and participate in<br>learning mobility and cooperation activities under Erasmus+. The award of<br>an ECHE represents the first stage in a two-stage submission procedure for<br>certain grants and does not trigger an immediate award of funding under<br>the Erasmus+ Programme. Higher Education institutions from the Western<br>Balkans third countries not associated to the programme can apply for and<br>be granted an ECHE for the purposes of the Call for Proposals on the<br>European Universities, to which they are eligible. The Charter outlines the<br>fundamental principles an institution should adhere to in organising and<br>implementing high quality mobility and cooperation. It states the requisites<br>the institution agrees to comply with to ensure high quality services and<br>procedures,as well as theprovision of reliable and transparent information.|
|**ECTS**<br>**(European**<br>**Credit**<br>**Transfer and Accumulation**<br>**System)**|A learner-centred system for credit accumulation and transfer, based on the<br>transparency of learning, teaching and assessment processes. Its objective is<br>to facilitate planning, delivery and evaluation of study programmes and<br>learner mobility through the recognition of qualifications and periods of<br>learning. A system that helps to design, describe and deliver study<br>programmes and award higher education qualifications. The use of ECTS, in<br>conjunction with outcomes-based qualifications frameworks, makes study<br>programmes and qualifications more transparent and facilitates the<br>recognition ofqualifications.|
|**Higher education institution**|Means an institution which, in accordance with national law or practice,<br>offers recognised degrees or other recognised tertiary level qualifications,<br>regardless of what such an establishment is called, or a comparable<br>institution at tertiary level which is considered by the national authorities as<br>eligible toparticipate in the Programme in their respective territories.|
|**Joint degree**|Single degree certificate awarded to a student upon successful completion<br>of a joint programme. The joint degree must be signed by the competent<br>authorities of two or more of the participating institutions jointly and<br>recognised officially in the countries where those participating institutions<br>are located.|
|**Joint programmes**|Higher education (study or research) programmes jointly designed,<br>delivered and fully recognised by two or more higher education institutions.<br>Joint programmes can be implemented at any higher education cycle, i.e.,<br>bachelor, master or doctorate or even short cycle. Joint programmes can be<br>national (i.e., when all universities involved are from the same country) or<br>transnational/international (i.e. when at least two different countries are<br>represented amongthe higher education institutions involved).|

452

|**One-cycle**<br>**programmes**|**study**|Integrated/long programmes leading either to a first or a second-cycle<br>degree and which, in some countries, can still be better characterised by<br>duration in years rather than credits. In most of these countries, the<br>programmes outside the Bologna first-cycle model are in the fields of<br>medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine, nursing and midwifery and in most<br>cases involve 1-8 % of the student population. The typical length of<br>integrated programmes leading to regulated professions is in general 300-<br>360 ECTS/five-sixyears dependingon the regulatedprofession inquestion.|
|---|---|---|
|**Third cycle**||The third cycle level in the Qualifications Framework for the European<br>Higher Education Area agreed by the ministers responsible for higher<br>education at their meeting in Bergen in May 2005 in the framework of the<br>Bologna process. The descriptor of the third cycle of the QF EHEA<br>corresponds to the learningoutcomes for EQF level 8.|

###### **Vocational Education and Training**<sup>**519**</sup>

|**Apprenticeship (Apprentice)**<br>**520**|Without prejudice to national terminology, apprenticeships are understood<br>as formal vocational education and training schemes that:<br>a) combine learning in education or training institutions with substantial<br>work-based learning in companies and other workplaces,<br>b) lead to nationally recognised qualifications,<br>c) are based on an agreement defining the rights and obligations of the<br>apprentice, the employer and, where appropriate, the vocational<br>education and training institution, and<br>d) include payment or other compensation to the apprentice for the<br>work-based component.|
|---|---|
|**EQAVET (European Quality**<br>**Assurance**<br>**Reference**<br>**Framework for Vocational**<br>**Education and Training)**|A reference tool for policy-makers based on a four-stage quality cycle that<br>includes goal setting and planning, implementation, evaluation and review.<br>It respects the autonomy of national governments and is a voluntary system<br>to be used by public authorities and other bodies involved in quality<br>assurance.|
|**VET skills competitions**|International sectoral events in which competitive demonstration of skills<br>by VET learners is central for promotion, recognition and exchange of<br>experience, know-how and technological innovations in VET. The events are<br>a result of close cooperation between businesses, VET providers, chambers<br>of commerce and other relevant stakeholders that aim at improving<br>attractiveness and excellence in VET, creating global training standards and<br>benchmarking systems, and influencing industry, government, and<br>educators through cooperation and research.<br>The purpose of skills competitions is to raise the profile and recognition of<br>skilled people and show how important skills are in achieving economic<br>growth and personal success. They are designed to inspire young people to<br>develop a passion for skills and pursuing excellence, through competitions<br>andpromotions.|

> 519  For other VET terminology please use the official Cedefop publication:  https://www.cedefop.europa.eu/files/4117_en.pdf

> 520 <u>https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32018H0502%2801%29</u>

453

|**Vocational education and**<br>**training (VET)**|Education and training which aims to equip young people and adults with<br>knowledge, skills and competences required in particular occupations or<br>more broadly on the labour market. It may be provided in formal and in non-<br>formal settings, at all levels of the European Qualifications Framework<br>(EQF), including tertiary level, if applicable. For the purpose of Erasmus+,<br>projects focusing on initial or continuing vocational education and training<br>are eligible under VET actions.|
|---|---|
|**Vocational education and**<br>**training (VET) learner**|A person enrolled in an initial or continuous vocational education and<br>training programme or a person who has recently graduated or obtained a<br>qualification from such aprogramme.|
|**Work-based learning**|Acquisition of knowledge and skills through carrying out – and reflecting on<br>– tasks in a vocational context, either at the workplace (such as alternance<br>training)or in a vocational education and traininginstitution.|

###### **Adult education**

|**Adult education**|All forms of non-vocational adult education, whether of a formal, non-<br>formal or informal nature(for continuous vocational trainingsee "VET").|
|---|---|
|**Adult learner**|Any adult who, having completed or being no longer involved in initial<br>education or training, returns to some forms of non-vocational continuing<br>learning (formal,non-formal or informal).|
|**h**<br>**Coach**|A resource person who is not a member of the group and who supports young<br>people in thepreparation,implementation and evaluation of theirproject.|
|**Community building**|Creation or enhancement of a community among individuals who share a common<br>need or interest or who lived a joint experience which created common ground.<br>The community created through the community building process is a lively group<br>of members who exchange practices and ideas for further development to the<br>benefit of the communityitself.|
|**Dialogue mechanisms**|Dialogue with young people and youth organisations and decision makers which<br>serves as a forum for continuous joint reflection on the priorities, implementation<br>and follow-upof European cooperation in theyouth field.|
|**Digital Youth Work**|Proactively using or addressing digital media and technology in youth work. Digital<br>media and technology can be either a tool, an activity or a content in youth work.<br>Digital youth work is not a youth work method, it can be included in any youth<br>work settingand it has the samegoals asyouth work ingeneral.|
|**Facilitator**|A person who helps a group of (young) people to work together better, understand<br>their common objectives, and plan how to achieve these objectives through<br>Erasmus+ activities|
|**Group Leader**|In youth mobility projects, an adult of at least 18 years of age who joins the young<br>people participating in a Youth Exchange in order to ensure their effective learning<br>(Youthpass), protection and safety.|

###### **Youth**

454

|**Informal group of young**<br>**people**|A group of at least four young people (13-30 years old) which does not have legal<br>personality under the applicable national law, provided that their group<br>representative has the legal capacity to undertake legal obligations on their behalf.<br>In case of a group which has minors, one of the members of the group who is at<br>least 18-years old assumes the role of representative and takes responsibility on<br>behalf of the group.<br>The group needs to be registered and validated in the Organisation Registration<br>System (ORS)<sup>521</sup>. For registration purposes, the formation of the group needs to be<br>evidenced by a registration form signed between the group members. The<br>signatures on the registration form may have to be officially authenticated, if<br>required by the granting authority, to ensure legal certainty. Existing groups which<br>are already registered in ORS also need to upload the signed registration form in<br>their ORS profile to be eligible to apply as an informal group of young people for<br>actions under the Call 2026 and onwards. The form can be downloaded from the<br>Organisation Registration System (ORS) as “Informal Group of Young People –<br>Registration Form”.<br>The informal groups of young people can be applicants and partners in some<br>actions of Erasmus+. For the purpose of simplification, they are assimilated to legal<br>persons (organisations, institutions, etc.) in this Guide and fit within the notion of<br>Erasmus+ participating organisations for Key Action 1 actions in which they can<br>takepart.|
|---|---|
|**Itinerant activity**|An activity taking place in more than one country. Itinerant activities imply the<br>movement of all participants at the same time.|
|**Local participant in youth**<br>**activities**|A participant in a learning mobility activity travelling less than 10 km to the venue<br>of the activity. Such participants are not eligible for travel support, but, depending<br>on the action, may be eligible for Individual Support, Organisational support and/or<br>Inclusion support.|
|**Smart Youth Work**|The innovative development of youth work encompassing digital youth work<br>practice and includinga research, qualityandpolicycomponent.|
|**Youth activity**|An out-of-school activity (such as a youth exchange, volunteering or youth training)<br>carried out by a young person, either individually or in a group, in particular<br>through youth organisations, and characterised by a non-formal learning<br>approach.|
|**Youth worker**|A professional or a volunteer involved in non-formal learning who supports young<br>people in theirpersonal socio-educational,andprofessional development.|
||The European tool to improve the recognition of the learning outcomes of young<br>people and youth workers from their participation in projects supported by the<br>Erasmus+ Programme. Youthpass consists of:<br>•<br>certificates that can be obtained by participants in several Actions of the<br>Programme; and|
|**Youthpass**|<br>•<br>a defined process which supports young people, youth workers and youth<br>organisations to reflect about the learning outcomes from an Erasmus+<br>project in the field of youth and non-formal learning. Youthpass is also<br>part of a broader European Commission strategy which aims to enhance<br>the recognition of non-formal and informal learning and of youth work in<br>Europe and beyond.|
